Eli (AE): Heads-up: Zenith's POC sees 429s + ~800ms TTFT on first call after their nightly CI deploy. They're asking if committed pricing is safe. Can we triage?
Vera (SRE): Can you drop a sample req id and whether they use the JS SDK?
Eli (AE): Sample req ztn-6a7f ts=2026-03-20T07:12:03Z. They run `redwood-js@0.9.2` in CI.
Rohit (Runtime): Two likely causes: 1) missing X-Customer-ID -> IP throttling, 2) cold KV cache on first few requests. 429 header should show `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0` if token bucket hit.
Eli (AE): Customer forwarded header showing remaining=0.
Vera (SRE): Quick mitigations: have them add `X-Customer-ID` in CI, run 3 warmup requests post-deploy, and patch to SDK >=0.9.4 to avoid aggressive retries. I can temporarily bump their burst +100 for 48h to stabilize.
Mai (Security): They also want our answer for key rotation and audit logs on the security questionnaire. I can provide a short statement about KMS support and rotation cadence.
Cal (Billing): For committed pricing we can propose a 3-month pilot with conditional conversion if TTFT <250ms and <0.5% 429s. Good?
Rohit (Runtime): If they add header + warmup we expect steady TTFT under 200ms. I'll file RDEV-6100 to add warmup to onboarding docs and RDEV-6101 to add per-customer preflight cache flag.
Vera (SRE): Burst bump applied for ztn-cust-id. Monitoring dashboard shows error-rate falling after their warmup run.
Eli (AE): Zenith ran warmup + SDK upgrade, new req ztn-6a80 TTFT ~160ms, no 429s in 30 calls. I'll send the pilot terms and security blurb.
Vera (SRE): Leaving the temporary bump for 48h and watching metrics.
Eli (AE): Thanks team, closing unless they regress.
